accuracy_quality_fields.value: Photogrammetry: Values in the higher-order products released in this dataset closely represent those of the observed surface. The images were acquired at high resolution from a professional-quality camera and lens. Accurate reproduction of surface values is a normal result when applying photogrammetry techniques, and additional preprocessing refinements were made by filtering outlier values of reprojection error, reconstruction uncertainty, and projection accuracy.

Photogrammetry: These data represent the movement sand ripples with a bi-modal grain-size distribution at the Grand Falls Dune Field (Navajo Nation, Arizona) between 02-20-2024 and 07-25-2024. All images used to generate the ripple DEMs were acquired at the same location within the dune field, approximately 50m south of weather station enclosure.

Photogrammetry: The data provided here contain values that are consistent with the expected range of values for sand ripples in a desert dune field. No data are duplicated, and the complete set of observations is included with this release. There is no geospatial data in this dataset, only non-projected point coordinates, so no topology tests were performed.

processing_lineage_fields.value: Photogrammetry: We used a NIKON D750 DSLR camera with a 35mm lens to acquire images of ripples in a ~60% overlapping pattern that completely surrounds the region of interest. Metashape processing: Camera alignment was performed using the highest accuracy option with no limits on the number of Key points or Tie points generated. The aligned point cloud was then optimized by individually filtering outlier values in projection error, reconstruction uncertainty and projection accuracy, in preparation for generation of a ‘dense’ point cloud. The dense cloud was generated using the ultra-high quality option and point colors were calculated. From the dense cloud, a mesh was generated as a height field (2.5D) using the high-face-count option with vertex colors calculated. Surface texture was created from the complete image set with a diffuse map generated by mosaicking and blending the images. Control points corresponding to the scale-bar marker distances were added, enabling relative geometry to be calculated and the DEM to be generated. The DEMs were generated based on the mesh with extrapolation enabled to fill any edge gaps. Based on each DEM, orthomosaic images were generated as image mosaics with pixel dimensions forced to match the corresponding DEM.
